authority: Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones
deadline_label: Before departure — at least 8 weeks ahead
non_obvious_official_guidance: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals exercise free movement rights and do not need a work permit. Non-EU nationals require a work and residence authorisation (autorización de residencia y trabajo) obtained by the Spanish employer before the employee departs.
non_obvious_actual_reality: EU nationals often assume no registration is needed for short assignments. Any stay exceeding 90 days triggers a mandatory registration obligation at the Oficina de Extranjería. Non-compliance does not block employment but creates a gap in the employee's legal status record and blocks access to the public health card (tarjeta sanitaria) and other municipal services.
non_obvious_action_required: Classify the employee's nationality before anything else. For EU/EEA nationals staying >90 days, book a cita previa (appointment) at the Oficina de Extranjería immediately — slots open 4–6 weeks out and fill within hours of release. For non-EU nationals, the employer must initiate the autorización application in Spain before travel; do not book flights until authorisation is confirmed.

non_obvious_official_guidance: Non-EU nationals must obtain a national long-stay visa (visado nacional, Tipo D) from the Spanish consulate in their country of residence before travelling to Spain to work. The employer's completed work authorisation is a prerequisite document.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Processing times vary dramatically by consulate — posts serving India, China, Morocco, and Pakistan routinely take 3–4 months. The Type D visa is valid for 90 days only and must be exchanged for a TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) after arrival. TIE appointment slots in Barcelona and Madrid fill within minutes of opening and are often unavailable for 8–12 weeks — HR must monitor TIE availability from the day of visa approval, not after the employee lands.
non_obvious_action_required: HR must track the consulate queue and TIE appointment availability simultaneously. Instruct the employee to attempt booking a TIE cita previa on the same day the visa is approved (not when it is collected). Build 4 months into the end-to-end timeline for high-demand consulates.
source: Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores – Visados nacionales

deadline_label: Within 3 months of establishing habitual residence
non_obvious_official_guidance: All residents in Spain — including foreign nationals — must register at their local Ayuntamiento in the Padrón Municipal. Registration requires proof of address (lease or property deed) and a valid identity document.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many landlords in major Spanish cities refuse to grant empadronamiento to tenants, fearing increased property tax liability or complications with short-term rental arrangements. Without landlord cooperation, employees are blocked from municipal registration — which in turn blocks opening a bank account, obtaining the tarjeta sanitaria, and enrolling children in school. Some Ayuntamientos accept a notarised declaration of residence as a workaround; others do not.
non_obvious_action_required: Before signing any lease, confirm in writing that the landlord will permit empadronamiento at the property — make it a contractual condition. If the landlord refuses post-arrival, escalate to the foreigners' desk (extranjería window) at the town hall rather than general reception; some municipalities have a procedure involving a municipal inspector visit to verify residence without landlord consent. Do not proceed to health card or bank account applications without a certified padrón certificate.

authority: Oficina de Extranjería / Comisaría de Policía Nacional
deadline_label: Within 3 months of arrival if staying >90 days
non_obvious_official_guidance: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals staying in Spain more than 3 months must register at the Oficina de Extranjería or designated Police station using form EX-18 and obtain a Certificado de Registro de Ciudadano de la Unión, which also assigns a NIE number.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The output document is an A4 paper certificate — not a plastic card. Many EU employees expect a card equivalent to their home country's residence permit and are unprepared for the paper format. The NIE number on it is permanent and is what is required for tax, banking, and contracts. Separately, if the employee needs the NIE urgently (e.g. to sign a lease before registration is complete), they can apply for a standalone NIE via form EX-15 at the same office or at a Spanish consulate abroad.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the cita previa before arrival if possible — slots open 4–8 weeks out. Bring: passport or national ID, completed EX-18 form, proof of address (padrón or lease), and the Tasa 790 código 012 government fee receipt (paid online before the appointment). The NIE is needed before opening a Spanish bank account or signing a property lease; do not leave this to week two.
source: Ministerio del Interior – Registro de ciudadanos de la UE en España

step: TIE – Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero (non-EU)
authority: Comisaría de Policía Nacional (Brigada Provincial de Extranjería)
deadline_label: Within 30 days of entry on national visa
non_obvious_official_guidance: Non-EU nationals who entered Spain on a Type D work visa must apply for a Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero (TIE) within 30 days of arrival at the provincial police headquarters. The TIE is the physical residence and identity card valid for the duration of the work authorisation.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 30-day statutory window and cita previa availability in Barcelona and Madrid are incompatible — appointment slots can stretch 6–10 weeks, leaving employees technically non-compliant through no fault of their own. The Spanish system tacitly accepts this but HR must document the appointment booking date to demonstrate good faith if audited. Biometric data must be given in person; no representative is accepted.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the TIE cita previa via sede.gob.es on the same day the Type D visa is approved. Screenshot the booking confirmation and file it as compliance evidence. If no appointment is available within 30 days, send written notification to the Oficina de Extranjería documenting the booking attempt. Bring to the appointment: passport and visa, two biometric photos, completed EX-17, work authorisation document, padrón certificate, and Tasa 790 fee receipt.
source: Ministerio del Interior – TIE para titulares de autorización de residencia

authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
field_label: Número de Afiliación a la Seguridad Social (NASS)
deadline_label: Before first working day — employer obligation
non_obvious_official_guidance: All workers in Spain must be registered with the TGSS and assigned a NASS before starting employment. The employer files form TA.1 (or the equivalent electronic procedure via Sistema RED) on behalf of the employee and must also file an alta (registration) before the employee's first shift.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The NASS and the NIE are distinct numbers — HR payroll teams frequently confuse them. If an employee has previously worked in Spain, their original NASS is permanent and does not need re-assigning; providing the wrong or duplicate number creates payroll reconciliation problems that take months to untangle. The alta must be filed before the first shift, not on it — a same-day registration is technically a violation.
non_obvious_action_required: Before Spanish payroll setup, ask the employee whether they have a prior NASS from any previous Spanish employment. If yes, provide the existing NASS to the payroll team immediately. For new affiliations, confirm the employer's payroll provider has Sistema RED access. File the alta the business day before the employee's first working day.
source: Seguridad Social – Afiliación, altas y bajas en el Sistema de Seguridad Social

step: Agencia Tributaria – NIF / Beckham Law Election
deadline_label: Modelo 149 election within 6 months of becoming tax resident
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals resident in Spain for tax purposes use their NIE as their NIF. Tax residency is triggered by spending more than 183 days in Spain in a calendar year, or by having Spain as the centre of vital economic interests. The AEAT administers all tax registrations and annual filings.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Spain's centre-of-vital-interests test can make an employee tax resident even with fewer than 183 days in-country if their principal business activities and assets are Spain-based — HR teams routinely miss this trigger for senior employees. Separately, the Beckham Law (régimen especial de trabajadores desplazados) allows newly tax-resident employees to elect taxation as non-residents at a flat 24% rate on Spanish-source income for up to 6 years — but the election via Modelo 149 must be filed within 6 months of first tax-residency registration and cannot be made retroactively. This is a one-time, time-limited option with significant tax savings for high earners.
non_obvious_action_required: Alert the employee and their tax adviser to the Beckham Law option within the first weeks of arrival. The 6-month deadline from tax-residency registration start is irrevocable. Confirm with payroll that the NIF loaded matches the NIE exactly — a mismatch between NIF and Seguridad Social records on payslips is an AEAT audit trigger.
source: Agencia Tributaria – Régimen especial trabajadores desplazados (Ley Beckham)

form_name: Application at assigned Centro de Salud
deadline_label: Within first month of empadronamiento and NASS activation
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees registered in the Social Security system and in the padrón municipal are entitled to a Tarjeta Sanitaria Individual (health card) from the regional public health system. The application is made at the locally assigned Centro de Salud.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Spain has 17 autonomous communities each running its own health system — procedures, card names, and document requirements vary by region. The physical NASS confirmation letter can take 4–6 weeks to arrive by post; employees who present only the letter and are in a region that does not accept digital TGSS printouts may be turned away at the Centro de Salud even though the number is live in the system.
non_obvious_action_required: Download a digital NASS confirmation from the TGSS Importass portal immediately after affiliation and bring it to the Centro de Salud instead of waiting for the physical letter. Verify the exact document list with the local Consejería de Sanidad — requirements in Madrid, Cataluña, and the Basque Country differ. Do not book health appointments until the tarjeta is confirmed active.
source: Ministerio de Sanidad – Tarjeta sanitaria individual

deadline_label: 1 April – 30 June following each tax year (Modelo 100); 30 June (Modelo 150)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Tax residents in Spain must file an annual personal income tax return (Declaración de la Renta) with the AEAT. Standard form is Modelo 100 for ordinary residents. Employees who elected the Beckham Law regime file Modelo 150.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Spain taxes worldwide income for tax residents — not just Spanish-source income. Employees with foreign bank accounts, pension funds, or investments above the Modelo 720 threshold must file a separate overseas asset declaration by 31 March. Many newly relocated employees are unaware their home-country pension or savings account creates a Spanish reporting obligation and discover it only during a tax inspection.
non_obvious_action_required: At year-end, have a Spanish tax adviser run a worldwide income assessment for every inbound tax resident — do not assume the AEAT's pre-filled draft (borrador) captures all income. Separately, check the Modelo 720 threshold (see es.modelo_720) before the 31 March deadline.
source: Agencia Tributaria – IRPF: Declaración de la Renta

field_label: Declaración de bienes y derechos en el extranjero
deadline_label: 31 March following the first year assets exceed €50,000 per category
non_obvious_official_guidance: Tax residents in Spain must declare overseas assets — bank accounts, securities, real estate, life insurance with savings components, and annuities — exceeding €50,000 per asset category by filing Modelo 720 with the AEAT annually by 31 March.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Modelo 720 is almost entirely unknown to newly relocated employees until they encounter it — often during a tax inspection. An employee with a family home, pension pot, and savings account in their home country can easily exceed the threshold in multiple categories without realising there is a Spanish filing obligation. ECJ Case C-788/19 (2022) struck down the disproportionate penalties, but Spain continues to levy administrative fines for late or missing declarations and conducts CRS automatic exchange matching to detect undisclosed foreign assets.
non_obvious_action_required: Screen for Modelo 720 exposure at onboarding by asking every inbound tax resident to list major foreign assets (property, pensions, bank accounts, investment portfolios). Have a Spanish tax adviser assess the per-category thresholds. Build the 31 March deadline into the HR compliance calendar alongside IRPF. The declaration must be repeated in any year the declared amount increases by more than €20,000 per category.
source: Agencia Tributaria – Modelo 720: Bienes y derechos en el extranjero

authority: Oficina de Extranjería / Comisaría de Policía Nacional
field_label: TIE Renewal Reference / New Expiry Date
deadline_label: Book cita previa 90 days before expiry; statutory window opens 60 days before
non_obvious_official_guidance: Non-EU nationals must renew their TIE before expiry. The statutory renewal application window opens 60 days before the card expiry date and is filed at the Oficina de Extranjería or online via sede.gob.es.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Cita previa slots for TIE renewal in Madrid, Barcelona, and Valencia are typically unavailable for 6–10 weeks. An employee who begins searching at the statutory 60-day mark will routinely find no appointment before the card expires. The employee is technically non-compliant during the gap even with proof of a pending renewal application, which can cause complications at border crossings.
non_obvious_action_required: Calendar TIE renewal at 90 days before expiry, not 60. On day 90, attempt the cita previa booking immediately and retain screenshots of failed attempts as compliance documentation. Brief the employee to carry the expired TIE alongside the renewal booking confirmation at all borders until the new card is issued.
source: Ministerio del Interior – Renovación de Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero

step: Social Security Totalization & Posted Worker Notification
authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social / home-country social security authority / Spanish Labour Inspectorate
form_name: A1 Certificate (EU postings) / Certificate of Coverage (bilateral treaty, non-EU)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Workers posted to Spain temporarily by a foreign employer may remain in their home-country social security system if an A1 certificate (EU postings, Regulation 883/2004) or certificate of coverage (bilateral treaty) is obtained before work begins in Spain. Without the certificate, Spanish Seguridad Social contributions apply from day one.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many HR teams assume EU free movement eliminates social security complexity for intra-EU postings. In practice, the A1 exemption has a maximum duration (typically 24 months, extendable with bilateral agreement) and must be applied for before the employee starts working in Spain — retroactive A1s are almost impossible to obtain. Additionally, a separate posted worker notification to the Spanish Labour Inspectorate via the RLC portal (Registro de Empresas Prestadoras de Servicios) is legally required before day one and is routinely missed.
non_obvious_action_required: For any intra-EU posting, apply for the A1 from the home-country social security authority before the employee's first day in Spain. File the posted worker notification on the Spanish RLC portal simultaneously — these are two separate obligations, not one. For non-EU nationals, confirm whether Spain has a bilateral totalization treaty with the employee's home country; if not, full Spanish Seguridad Social contributions apply from day one.
source: Seguridad Social – Desplazamiento temporal de trabajadores y certificado A1
